mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.8% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.8% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of at least 0.3 percentage points within the same month signals a tightening labor market, which boosts wage pressures and ultimately leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month by at least 0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous year's average for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous year average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPI inflation above 4%, signals aggressive monetary tightening in a high-inflation environment, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.75pp AND CPIAUCSL > 4.0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the trajectory of real GDP growth (GDPC1) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days; higher quarterly GDP growth is associated with higher equity returns in the subsequent two months.
failure_condition: The correlation between quarterly GDPC1 growth and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample testing.
